title: An instance can carry Active status while its rate limits are set to zero, making it configured but dormant
content:
The Aave container states that "the Ethereum Mainnet Instances of the Aave Protocol with `Active` Status are stored herein" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.2). The Aave Prime USDS instance filed inside it publishes inflow rate limits of "`maxAmount`: 0, `slope`: 50,000,000 USDS per day" (.2.1.2.4.1) and outflow rate limits of "`maxAmount`: 0, `slope`: Unlimited" (.2.1.2.4.2).

With `maxAmount` at zero, no amount can pass the `rateLimited` check regardless of slope — a bucket with zero capacity never holds anything to spend. The instance is complete in every other respect: network, target protocol, supplied asset USDS, receipt token `aEthLidoUSDS`, token and underlying addresses all populated.

So `Active` here classifies *approval and specification*, not *operability*. The venue has passed whatever review the Artifact requires and is standing by; enabling it later is a single parameter change to `maxAmount` at a known Atlas address, not a new governance drafting exercise.

This separation is efficient but creates a genuine reading hazard. Anyone inventorying live exposure from the Active/Inactive taxonomy alone would count Aave Prime USDS as a live conduit, and anyone estimating capacity from `slope` would see 50,000,000 USDS per day. Only the `maxAmount` of 0 reveals the instance is inert — a case where the operative fact sits in the least prominent field, and where status labels and effective parameters can point in opposite directions.
description: Aave Prime USDS is filed under Active Instances yet publishes maxAmount 0 for both inflow and outflow, so the venue is fully specified and pre-approved without any capacity to move capital.
